Function hash_through 

Source 
pub fn hash_through<S, H, F>(
    cache: &Mutex<HashCache>,
    stamps: &S,
    path: &str,
    mode: HashVerifyMode,
    location: &FileLocation,
    compute: F,
) -> Result<Through, ThroughError<S::Error, H>>
where
    S: FileStamp,
    F: FnMut(&S::File) -> Result<CacheValue, H>,
Expand description

Gets the value for the file at path from cache, or computes it.

  1. The file is opened once (FileStamp::open). Everything after uses that handle, so a link or junction swapped mid-way cannot pair one file’s key with another file’s content.
  2. The handle is stamped. If mode allows (HashVerifyMode::must_recompute) and the cache has a valid value for that key, it is returned and the file is not read.
  3. Otherwise the handle is rewound (FileStamp::rewind), compute hashes it from its first byte, and the handle is stamped again. compute may be called more than once on the same handle. If the two stamps differ, the file changed while it was read: the hash is thrown away and retried, up to MAX_UNSTABLE_RETRIES times. Then the result is Through::Unstable, and any entry for the file is dropped.
  4. A value whose flat hashes cover a different size than the key records is never cached; it is Through::Unstable too.
  5. A stable value is cached and returned.

Under a recompute mode the cache is consulted without counting a lookup (HashCache::peek), and only to set cache_disagreed. That compares the flat SHA-256 of an entry for the same key as the fresh hash, and only when both have one.

The lock is held only to look up and to insert, never while hashing. The time spent hashing and the bytes hashed are added to the metrics.
